CAUSE: `bash()` enforces the timeout on `proc.communicate()`, but its cleanup can wait forever for a descendant to close the captured output pipe.

Evidence: [tools.py](/home/kesha/bench906/runs/A-T8-luna-r1/app/harness/tools.py:157) handles the timeout by calling `_kill_proc(proc)` and then awaiting the `communicate()` reader at line 159. In [bg_jobs.py](/home/kesha/bench906/runs/A-T8-luna-r1/app/bg_jobs.py:248), `_cleanup_pidfd_group()` polls whether the process group is alive. A command that backgrounds a child which inherits stdout can leave that child running after its shell leader exits. The process group remains alive, but `proc.communicate()` waits for the inherited pipe to close. The cleanup polling therefore keeps waiting, so the nominal timeout is exceeded without a return.

Recommend making timeout cleanup bounded and ensuring it cannot wait indefinitely for pipe EOF. For example, kill the owned process group promptly on timeout, then drain the reader with a bounded wait and cancel it if descendants still hold the pipe. Test with a command whose background child inherits stdout.
